comment: The <<} of a comment that opened on an earlier line. Markdown's paragraph rule starts again at each line, which ends the comment's span from manuscript-markdown.json there, so its <<} is in no comment's span. Here it's scoped as the comment's closer, so it shows as one, and its } is a comment's, which no bracket pairs with. Inside a comment's span this injects nothing, so the comment's own end pattern pairs its <<}, and a reply's, as {>>note {>>reply<<}<<}, on one line. Nor does it inject in an indented code block or an HTML comment, whose <<} is theirs, though it can't tell a <<} of no comment in a paragraph's text, as in a <pre> block, which Markdown's grammar reads as the paragraph's text, or after an escaped {, from a comment's, and takes it as one. A comment's <<} on a line indented four spaces after a blank line, at the top level, is in Markdown's indented code block, so it shows as the code's.
